title: 第三章 法治政体中的超法律权威
originalTitle: 3 Extralegal Authority in a Lawful Polity

zh: 本章将考察法律及其界限在界定罗马—拜占庭共和国概念与运作中的作用。人们有一种共识：真正的

必须由法律来统治，但这如何与一位能够颁布、修改、废止或无视法律的君主的存在相调和？这造成了一种表面上的矛盾：皇帝是受制于法律，还是高于法律？两种意见都有人表达，致使现代法律学者陷入僵局。本文将论证，部分问题在于我们未能把法律与皇帝都置于共和国的关系中来界定，而共和国先于二者、也重于二者。此外，皇帝并非唯一能够“合法地”行动于法律之外的人：人民也能如此，尤其当他们决定废黜一位皇帝时，因为共和国终究是他们的。
en: This chapter will examine the role of law and its limits in defining the Roman-Byzantine concept and operation of the republic. There was a consensus that a true

has to be ruled by law, but how could this be reconciled with the existence of a monarch who could issue, change, annul, or ignore the laws? This created an apparent contradiction: was the emperor subject to or above the law? Both opinions were expressed, which had led to an impasse among modern legal scholars. Part of the problem, it will be argued, is that we have failed to define both the law and the emperor in relation to the republic, which was prior to and more important than either. Moreover, the emperor was not the only one who could “legitimately” act beyond the laws: the people could do so too, especially when they decided to depose an emperor, for the republic was theirs, after all.

zh: “法治政体”的理想
en: The Ideal of the “Lawful Polity”

zh: 484年，皇帝利奥一世（457–474年在位）的遗孀、在位皇帝泽农（Zenon，474–491年在位）的岳母维里娜（Verina），当时在塔尔索斯（Tarsos）受叛军将领伊洛斯（Illos）控制，经他说服，宣布拥立莱昂提奥斯（Leontios）为帝。这只是一系列不断变换的联盟中的一个时刻，但我们将聚焦于维里娜致安条克（Antioch）人民、宣告她支持莱昂提奥斯的那封信。信文如下：
en: In 484, Verina, widow of the emperor Leon I (457–474) and mother-in-law of the reigning emperor Zenon (474–491), was persuaded by the rebel general Illos, who held her in his power at Tarsos, to proclaim a certain Leontios emperor. This was only one moment in a series of shifting alliances, but we will focus on the letter that Verina sent to the people of Antioch proclaiming her support for Leontios. It read as follows:

zh: “埃利亚·维里娜（Ailia Verina），永恒的奥古斯塔（Augusta），致我们安条克的公民们。须知在蒙福的利奥死后，皇帝权威归于我们。我们曾立斯特拉科迪塞奥斯（Strakodisseos）为帝，他后来被称为泽农，以造福我们的臣民与全体军队。但如今我们看见
连同我们的臣民正被他的贪婪所毁，因此我们认为有必要为你们加冕一位虔诚的、以正义为饰的皇帝，以便他拯救罗马
的事务、促使我们的敌人归于和平、并依法律使全体臣民得以安稳。我们已加冕最虔诚的莱昂提奥斯，他将照料你们每个人，也会为你们的需要作打算。”安条克全体民众立刻一致奋起，高呼：“上帝伟大！求主怜悯，为我们行善与至善之事。”
en: “Ailia Verina, perpetual Augusta, to our citizens of Antioch. Know that the imperial authority, after the death of the blessed Leon, is ours. We made Strakodisseos emperor, who was afterwards called Zenon, to benefit our subjects and all the military units. But now we see that the
and along with it our subjects, being ruined by his greed, and so we have deemed it necessary to crown a pious emperor for you who is adorned with justice so that he may save the affairs of the Roman

induce our enemies to be at peace, and make secure all the subjects in accordance with the laws. We have crowned Leontios the most pious, who will deem you all worthy of his care and providence.” And the entire populace of Antioch immediately rose up as one and cried out, “God is Great! and Lord have mercy, do what is good and best for us.”

zh: 这封信反映了关于

的愿望，此处它同时被称为
与

普遍同意的批准，帝国行动唯一可允许的动机就是

而被废黜。维里娜明确说她的选择莱昂提奥斯将依法律治理。这是我们将在这节及下一节讨论的一个关键标准。最后，道德品质与宗教仅被用来把潜在“好”皇帝与过去的“坏”皇帝区分开来（虔诚对贪婪）。奥古斯塔与其臣民的关系中没有任何神学成分；它不运作于皇帝与上帝之间的空间。
en: This letter reflects a number of fundamental assumptions about the workings of the

and the relationship between emperors and subjects. Verina had to persuade her subjects to accept her decision, and to that end she needed to deploy precisely the arguments that most closely corresponded to the prevalent ideology concerning the use and purpose of imperial power. She had to create a new consensus by identifying and appealing to the expectations that her subjects had of her. In this regard, her position was no different than that of any emperor ruling in peace. These, then, are the assumptions reflected in her letter: Communication is imagined as taking place between imperial authority and an undifferentiated body of citizens (the
of Antioch). It is deemed successful when it is greeted by a universal consensus among them, who are here called “the entire populace” (δῆμος =

). We may be skeptical of whether that actually happened, though it certainly may have. What is more important is that this was how imperial communication was represented as successful. In other words, imperial legitimacy was established by universal popular consent. The sole motive that Verina alleges for both the elevation of Zenon and his deposition (and the elevation of Leontios) is her desire to benefit the
called here both
and
Therefore, for imperial decisions to be ratified by the universal consent of the
the only allowable motive for imperial action was the good of the
As far as ideological parameters go, these were universal in Byzantium too, as we have seen. Also, an emperor could be deposed for failing to do right by the

Verina specifies that her choice, Leontios, will govern according to the laws. This a key criterion that we will discuss in this and the following section. Finally, moral qualities and religion are invoked only to distinguish potentially “good” emperors from past “bad” ones (piety versus greed). There is nothing theological in the relationship between the Augusta and her subjects; it does not operate in the space between emperor and God.

zh: 无论作为一篇帝国修辞还是作为罗马史上的一个事件，这一沟通的框架方式都没有任何激进、革命乃至不寻常之处。第1章考察过的利奥六世
旨在达到同样的修辞诉求标准，尽管他擢升与废降的是法律而非皇位候选人。维里娜很难用别的措辞来框架她的诉求；她必须说出皇帝和臣民都早已深信不疑的原则，即罗马的权力应当如何行使。当然，我们不必相信这出戏中所有角色都个人性地受这些观念驱动，正如任何政治家做事都不单为其选民的善。我们感兴趣的是政治领域的构成，是皇帝们必须做什么才能首先被认作合法的皇帝。
en: There was nothing radical, revolutionary, or even unusual in how this communication was framed, either as a piece of imperial rhetoric or as an event in Roman history. Leon VI’s

examined in Chapter 1, aimed to meet the same standards of rhetorical appeal, though he was elevating and demoting laws rather than candidates for the throne. It would have been difficult for Verina to frame her appeal in different terms; she had to express shared assumptions about the exercise of Roman power that were already hardwired into both emperors and subjects. Of course, we do not need to believe that all the characters in this drama were personally motivated by these notions, no more than any politicians do what they do solely for the good of their constituents. What we are interested in is the constitution of the political sphere, what emperors had to do to be recognizable as legitimate emperors in the first place.

zh: 我从无数类似时刻中选出维里娜致安条克人的信来讨论，是因为她以泽农辜负

该书以残篇传世，其中最长最著名的一段记述了449年出使阿提拉（Attila）的一次使团，普里斯科斯随行。使团从君士坦丁堡行至匈人帝国边界，再向北，深入罗马人会视为文明世界之外的地方，抵达阿提拉的宫廷。在外交谈判的背景下，讲究文学表达的历史作者普里斯科斯叙述了他在那里与一位讲希腊语的罗马流亡者（一个

之基本原则、优长与缺陷的辩论。
这位逃亡者化身了退出
的可能性、条件与后果，而普里斯科斯把辩论置于阿提拉营地的决定使替代方案的存在变得可感。在君士坦丁堡哪怕提出这个问题都可能显得荒唐，更不用说辩论它了。
en: I selected Verina’s letter to the Antiochenes for discussion from among countless similar moments because her attempt to depose Zenon on the grounds that he had failed the
happened around the same time that Priskos of Panion published his
(probably in the late 470s).

The work survives in fragments, of which the longest and most famous recounts an embassy to Attila in 449 that Priskos accompanied. The group traveled from Constantinople to the borders of the Hun empire and then north, well outside what the Romans would have deemed the civilized world, to the court of Attila. Against the backdrop of diplomatic negotiations, Priskos, a literary historian, narrates an encounter that he had there with a Greek-speaking Roman expatriate (a
yet another Hellenized Latin word). If not outright invented by Priskos, the encounter was elaborated by him to become a debate on the fundamental principles, merits, and flaws of the Roman
The fugitive incarnated the possibility, conditions, and consequences of opting out of the

while Priskos’s decision to situate the debate at the camp of Attila made the presence of alternatives palpable. It might have seemed ludicrous to even raise the question in Constantinople, much less debate it.

zh: 这位
在匈人中过得不错。他向普里斯科斯解释，他曾在一次劫掠中被俘，但在一场战争中很好地服役于其主人，并用战利品赎买了自由。显然，他觉得有必要解释自己为何随后选择留在匈人中，于是发起对罗马生活的猛烈抨击：人们不被允许携带武器自卫，将领们无能；税赋沉重；腐败无处不在；法律适用不平等，因为富人设法脱罪、审判拖得太久、还得给法官付钱。普里斯科斯在回应中并不争辩这些事没有发生。他把这段交流收入
的部分原因，正是借他人之口宣泄这些批评。相反，他把讨论带到更深的层面，带到“罗马人的
”所赖以建立的原则。他提出，这些原则是明智的，因为它们要求军事、司法与农业职能的分离，每一职能都对整体的运作作出自己的贡献。这些群体各自都“守卫”或“监督”
的不同面向。拜占庭摘录者对该段的压缩使部分论述难以跟随，但似乎普里斯科斯是沿着苏格拉底（Sokrates）在
）中的论证路线来捍卫整个体制的正义的，该论证把正义与职能分离相联系。普里斯科斯关心的是捍卫基本原则的正义，即便他知道这些原则并不总以最好的方式被落实。他甚至断言“法律适用于所有人，连皇帝也服从它们”。
下文我们将看到这是一个难点。
en: This Graikos had done well among the Huns. He explains to Priskos that he had been captured in a raid but had served his owner well in a war and had purchased his freedom from the spoils. Obviously, he feels compelled to explain why he had then chosen to remain among the Huns and launches into a tirade against Roman life: people are not allowed to bear arms for their own defense and the generals are no good; taxes are heavy; there is corruption everywhere; and the laws are not applied equally, as the rich manage to get off, trials last too long, and one has to pay the judges. In his response, Priskos does not argue that these things do not happen. Part of the reason he included the exchange in his
was to air these criticisms through someone else’s mouth. Instead, he takes the discussion to a deeper level, to the principles on which “the

of the Romans” was founded. These, he proposes, were wise, as they required the separation of military, judicial, and agricultural functions, each of which made its own contribution to the workings of the whole. Each of these classes “guarded” or “supervised” a different aspect of the

The condensation of the passage by the Byzantine excerptor makes it difficult to follow parts of the exposition, but it seems that Priskos defended the justice of the entire system along the lines of Sokrates’s argument in the

which links justice to separation of functions. Priskos is concerned to defend the justice of the fundamental principles even if he knows that they are not always implemented in the best way. He goes so far as to assert that “the laws apply to all, and even the emperor obeys them.”
We will see below that this was a difficult point.

zh: 普里斯科斯随后把讨论转到这位
自己在匈人中的处境，从而反将一军。“至于你的自由，你该感谢命运。”他在被俘期间或在他赢得自由的那场战斗中，任何事都可能发生。他是运气好。匈人中的生活显然受运气、受一个专制者任意意志的支配，而这可以是阿提拉的隐喻。相比之下，在罗马人那里，有关于如何对待奴隶的法律，且“他们中间有许多被认可的授予自由的方式”。此时，“我的相识哭了，说法律是公平的、罗马人的
是好的，但当权者不像古人那样为它着想，正在毁掉它。”
普里斯科斯随后说他们的讨论被打断了，这意味着该问题在某些方面仍然开放。显然他意图让读者思考
的运作与维护得以改进的途径。他几乎借
之口列出了一份改革议程。总体而言，

在实际中的运作方式，而普里斯科斯捍卫其许多安排背后的原则，同时承认它们并不总按应有的方式运作。
en: Priskos then turns the tables on the Graikos by bringing the discussion to his own circumstances among the Huns. “As for your freedom, you should give thanks to Chance.” Anything could have happened to him in captivity or in the battle where he earned his freedom. He got lucky. Life among the Huns is apparently governed by luck, the arbitrary whim of a despot, which could be a metaphor for Attila. With the Romans, by contrast, there are laws about how one can treat slaves and “there are many sanctioned ways of giving freedom among them.” At this point, “my acquaintance wept and said that the laws were fair and the
of the Romans was good, but that the authorities were ruining it by not taking the same thought for it as had those of old.”

Priskos then says that their discussion was interrupted, signifying that the question in some respects remains open. Clearly he intended his readers to think about the ways in which the functioning and maintenance of the
could be improved. He virtually lays out an agenda for reform through the mouth of the Graikos. Generally, the Graikos attacks the way the
operates in practice while Priskos defends the principles behind many of its arrangements, conceding that they do not always work the way they were supposed to.

zh: 我们能从这段文字得出什么结论？其一：罗马人的
概念是一种理想的抽象，对照它，当下的实践可能显得不足。个别罗马人可以诉诸
的原则来倡导改革，但皇帝同样可以如此，正如我们在第1章利奥六世那里所见。此外，
并非由政府行动或帝国体制所构成；相反，它是先于它们的东西，由整个社会所构成，其要素依照共享的正义原则进入了相互依存的关系。这些原则在法律中被表达与显现，而普里斯科斯要把皇帝们置于它们之下。我们将在下一节考察拜占庭如何处理这个特定问题。
en: What conclusions can we draw from this passage? One is that the concept of the
of the Romans was an ideal abstraction compared to which current practice could be found wanting. Individual Romans could invoke the principles of the
to advocate reform, but the same could be done by emperors, as we saw with Leon VI in Chapter 1. Moreover, the

is not constituted by government action or the imperial system; instead, it is something prior to them, constituted by the whole of society whose elements have entered into relations of mutual codependence according to shared principles of justice. These principles are expressed and manifested in the laws and Priskos wants to subordinate the emperors to them. We shall examine in the next section how this particular question was approached in Byzantium.

一词有时可被用来意指“国家”并应用于任何外国政权，但拜占庭作家在意指“罗马方式的政体”即一个依法组织的政体时，也可以表述得很清楚。
让我们考虑两个例子。

among the Huns. Their world was governed by chance, or the whim of a despot, not by established laws and customs to which all adhere. Perhaps the Graikos weeps at the end because he recognizes the precarious situation that he finds himself in. The advantages of a
emerge strongly even from what Priskos does
say. There can be no
of the Huns, not so much because of who the Huns were (Priskos depicts them as rather civilized, in their own way), but because of the stringent requirements needed to have a

as Cicero and others had explained them and as the Byzantines understood them. Having any kind of state or social and political power structure did not mean that you also had a lawful polity. While the word
could sometimes be used to mean “state” and applied to any foreign power, Byzantine writers could also be clear when they meant “a polity in the Roman manner,” that is, a lawfully constituted one.
Let us consider two examples.

en: They are not nomads like the other Hunnic peoples, but for a long period have been established in a rich land... They are the only Huns who have white bodies and faces that are not ugly. It is also true that their manner of living is unlike that of their kinsmen, nor do they live a savage life as they do; but they are ruled by one king, and since they possess an
they observe right and justice in their dealings both with one another and with their neighbors, in no degree less than the Romans and the Persians.

与其他任何类型的权力形态区分开来的一种方式。这是一个我们将在下文经常遇到的技术术语。普罗科匹乌斯在此暗示嚈哒、罗马与波斯各自拥有自己的

en: (“lawful polity”) was one way to differentiate a

along Roman lines from any other type of power formation. It is a technical term that we will encounter often below. Prokopios is here suggesting that the Ephthalitai, Romans, and Persians each had their own

and bases this verdict on the relations of justice that they maintain among and between them and also on their level of what we loosely call civilization. Roman imperial authorities of his time recognized the Persian empire as a state on a par with Rome and treated it more or less as an equal.
Prokopios’s successor and continuer, Agathias (writing in ca. 580), admitted that he did not know any other
that had changed so many “formations” and “shapes” as had the Persian one over the long course of its history,
but he still treated it as a peer polity. The historian Theophylaktos, writing in the seventh century, grants the dignity of the name
only to the Romans and the Persians.

zh: 阿加提阿斯专门用一段插叙记述法兰克人（Franks）社会，聚焦的正是以罗马规范为参照，应如何理解他们的
en: Agathias devoted a digression to the society of the Franks, focusing precisely on the nature of their
in relation to Roman norms.

zh: 法兰克人不像某些蛮族那样是游牧者，而是其
与法律以罗马模式为范本，除此之外他们在契约、婚姻与宗教奉行方面坚持类似的标准。他们事实上全是基督徒，且秉持最严格的正统。他们城中也有官长与祭司，并以与我们相同的方式庆祝节日；而且，作为一个蛮族民族，他们给我的印象是极有教养、极文明，除粗陋的衣着风格与奇特的语言外几乎与我们相同。我钦佩他们的其他品质，尤其盛行于他们中间的正义与和谐精神。
en: The Franks are not nomads, as some barbarians are, but their

and laws are modeled on the Roman pattern, apart from which they uphold similar standards with regard to contracts, marriage and religious observance. They are in fact all Christians and adhere to the strictest orthodoxy. They also have magistrates in their cities and priests and celebrate the feasts in the same way as we do; and, for a barbarian people, strike me as extremely well-bred and civilized and as practically the same as us except for their uncouth style of dress and peculiar language. I admire them for their other attributes and especially for the spirit of justice and harmony which prevails amongst them.

zh: 我们反复发现，并非每个国家或民族都够格称为
。罗马标准被用作与其他民族比较的基准。我们再次遇到政体不能由游牧民族构成的主张。政体需要法律以及宗教与公共行政的社会纽带：法治政体的统治者必须遵守一套由人民公共共识批准的共同标准，而非单纯跟随自己的意志。法兰克人在语言与衣着上不同，因为他们是与罗马人不同的民族、不同的民族文化，但依照阿加提阿斯这一虚构的呈现，他们满足了一个正当政体的形式要求。
en: Repeatedly we find that not every state or people qualify as a

Roman standards are used as a benchmark in comparisons with other peoples. Again we encounter the claim that polities cannot be constituted by nomadic peoples. Polities require laws and the social bonds of religion and public administration: the rulers of lawful polities must adhere to a common set of standards ratified by the public consensus of a people, and not simply follow their whim. The Franks differ in their language and dress because they are a different people from the Romans, a different national culture, but according to this fictional presentation by Agathias they fulfill the formal requirements of a proper polity.

zh: 这些同时也是政治理论家的历史学家，并非为外国政体本身而谈论它们。他们撰写这些插叙主要是作为对罗马政体状况的间接反思，正如普里斯科斯借一个匿名陌生人之口宣泄对罗马公共政策的严肃批评。这种颠覆效果部分由他们关于嚈哒与法兰克社会所做的荒谬主张所触发，这些主张应当引起大多数读者的警觉。
但在此过程中他们揭示了他们认为任何正当
都应具备的一般品质。我还注意到，他们的构想根本上是世俗的。宗教重要，因为它是民族文化的一部分，但政体本身则取决于成员之间是否形成了合乎正义的关系。波斯人不是基督徒，但他们有政体；罗马
本身的奠基者也不是基督徒。
en: These historians, who were also political theorists, were not talking about foreign polities for their own sake. They crafted these digressions primarily as indirect reflections on the state of the Roman polity, much as Priskos employed an anonymous stranger to vent serious criticisms of Roman public policy. This subversive effect is triggered in part by the preposterous claims that they make about Ephthalite and Frankish society, which should alert most readers.
But in the process they reveal the general qualities that they thought should be found in any proper

I note also that their conception was fundamentally secular. Religion is important because it is part of the national culture, but the polity itself is a function of relations of justice. The Persians were not Christians, but they had a polity; nor had the founders of the Roman
itself been Christians.

zh: 罗马政体应当具有守法的秩序。法律旨在促进共同体价值、保护公共善免受私人利益侵害。这是可以把蛮族区分出来的一个标准。奥罗西乌斯（Orosius，五世纪早期）记述了一则来历无从证实、却颇能说明问题的轶事。阿陶尔夫（Athaulf）作为阿拉里克（Alaric）之后哥特人的国王，曾考虑抹去罗马之名、干脆以
取代
，但当他考虑到哥特人根本无法服从任何法律时改变了主意，且“他认为剥夺一个政体的法律是错误的（没有法律，政体就根本不是政体）”。
en: A Roman polity was supposed to have a lawful order. Laws aimed to promote community values and protect the common good from private interests. This was a standard by which barbarians could be distinguished. Orosius (early fifth century) relates a revealing apocryphal anecdote. Athaulf, the successor of Alaric as king of the Goths, had considered obliterating the Roman name and simply replacing
with
but changed his mind when he considered that the Goths could simply not obey any law and “he believed it wrong to deprive a polity of laws (without which a polity is not a polity at all).”

zh: 在第1章，我们考察了拜占庭历史学家如何想象其政体从君主制到共和国、再回到君主制的过渡。他们中有些人从法律角度看待那段历史。约安尼斯·吕多斯（Ioannes Lydos，六世纪）坚持一个正当的
必须是
，否则就只是僭主制。他从这一立场撰写罗马共和国史，但他的历史也像历史学家们的插叙一样是论战性的。他想论证的是查士丁尼是一个僭主，且罗马政体自执政官时代以来已经衰落，而执政官曾与法律一道是其自由的堡垒。
法律所保障的自由，其对立面就是任由查士丁尼或阿提拉这样的专制者摆布。同样的观念弥漫于普罗科匹乌斯的
，该文本可能为吕多斯所知。普罗科匹乌斯聚焦于查士丁尼对法律体制的系统性滥用、他不遵守旧的好法律、以及他为服务暂时利益而通过坏的新法律。
的目标之一正是要说明，皇帝的任性如今已
法律。正是他在法律领域的不断创新使查士丁尼在普罗科匹乌斯眼中成为僭主。
的对立面是奴役，是失去由法律保障的自由。这正是塞奥多拉（Theodora）之类的人无法理解或尊重的东西。普罗科匹乌斯把她呈现为持有一种彻底个人化的权力观；她不知道非人格的
为何物：“
由此被降为一个奴隶栏，而她是我们在奴性上的教师。”
所有这些都是对查士丁尼自己宣告的有针对性的回应，后者在宣告中夸耀他已把自由恢复给罗马人，并承认
的基础是法律。
en: In Chapter 1, we looked at how Byzantine historians imagined the transition of their polity from monarchy to Republic and then back to monarchy. Some of them viewed that history from a legal aspect. Ioannes Lydos (in the sixth century) insisted that a proper
had to be an

or else it was just a tyranny. He wrote the history of the Roman republic from this standpoint, but his history too, like the digressions in the historians, was polemical. What he wanted to argue was that Justinian was a tyrant and that the Roman polity had declined from the time of the consuls, who, along with the laws, had once been the bulwarks of its freedom.
The opposite of lawful freedom was subjection to the whim of a despot such as Justinian (or Attila). The same notion pervades Prokopios’s

a text possibly known to Lydos. Prokopios focuses on Justinian’s systematic abuse of the legal system, his failure to adhere to the old good laws, and his passage of bad new ones to serve his temporary advantage. One of the goals of the
was to show precisely that whim had now
law. It was his constant innovation in the field of law that made Justinian a tyrant in Prokopios’s eyes. The opposite of a

was slavery, the loss of the freedom that was guaranteed by the laws. It was precisely this that people such as Theodora could not understand or respect. Prokopios presents her as having a thoroughly personal view of power; she had no idea what an impersonal
was: “The
was thereby reduced to a slave-pen and she was our teacher in servility.”
All this was a targeted response to Justinian’s own proclamations, in which the emperor boasted that he had restored freedom to the Romans and also recognized that the basis of the
was law.

zh: 吕多斯与普罗科匹乌斯的抱怨当然夸大了，正如佐纳拉斯与科尼阿特斯对科穆宁家族的抱怨（我们在第2章考察过）一样。罗马人的共和国并未被查士丁尼不可挽回地摧毁，正如后来也未由科穆宁家族摧毁。这些作者是在参与一种罗马论战传统。例如，西塞罗曾有一个著名的信念：“真正的
”早在他之前就已毁坏。他让他笔下的说话者西庇阿·埃米利安努斯（Scipio Aemilianus，公元前二世纪）说：“并非由于某种偶然——不，而是由于我们自己的道德缺陷——我们才只剩下
之名，而其实质早已丧失。”
普罗科匹乌斯、吕多斯与佐纳拉斯说的是同一件事。共和国总是在被摧毁与被恢复。奥古斯都在西塞罗之后恢复了它，查士丁二世在查士丁尼之后恢复了它。
共和国在内战之后、或当新皇帝想要标示方向转变时被恢复。
这种反复是罗马政治辞令中长久存在的模式，也是构成这种辞令的一部分。
en: The complaints of Lydos and Prokopios were exaggerated, of course, as were the complaints of Zonaras and Choniates against the Komnenoi (which we examined in Chapter 2). The republic of the Romans had not been irrevocably destroyed by Justinian any more than it was later by the Komnenoi. These authors were participating in a tradition of Roman polemic. Cicero, for example, famously believed that the “true

” had been destroyed long before his own time. His makes his speaker Scipio Aemilianus (second century BC) say that “it is not by some accident—no, it is because of our own moral failings—that we are left with the name of the
having long since lost its substance.”
Prokopios, Lydos, and Zonaras were saying the same thing. The republic was always being destroyed and restored. Augustus restored it after Cicero, and Justin II restored it after Justinian.
The republic was restored after civil wars or when new emperors wanted to signal a change of direction.
This was a persistent rhythm in Roman political rhetoric, indeed constitutive of it.

zh: 为聚焦法律问题，我提请注意一部匿名而晦涩的三页罗马法史，可能写于十一世纪晚期。“须知，”该文本说，“在罗马的最初开端与生成之时，当罗慕路斯（Romulus）统治时，
没有法律……当
再次掌权时，它依赖一种模糊的法律与习惯，而非依照法律作为
运作。”然而最终，他们组成了十人委员会，“以在法律中奠定罗马
的基础”。
该论著包含一些对早期罗马史的离奇误解（例如
统治于
之下），但它提出了一个政体如何变得守法的有趣模型：王政时代无法律，早期共和国起初是习惯法，后来才是正式法律。第二阶段与利奥六世关于习惯如何在获得他正式批准之前就能构成一个政体的看法有理论亲缘性，这是一种非官方的
的奇特形式，正如该文本为早期共和国所提议的那样。然而所有这些都引出了一个问题：守法政体在帝国君主制之下的地位如何。不幸的是，该文本在这一点上混乱。它声称“随着时间推移
增长，案件与审判的数量也增长……于是在恺撒·奥古斯都之下，
的不同群体开始制定法律，平民与更精选者皆然，连同将领、智者与
（裁判官）”。不清楚作者这里在想什么。无论如何，像大多数罗马人一样，他不相信拥有皇帝与拥有守法政体之间有任何冲突。那么，拜占庭人如何想象一个至高君主能够统治一个
而不使其沦为由意志支配的僭主制？专制与法治之间难道没有一种根本张力吗？
en: To focus on the question of law, I draw attention to an anonymous and obscure three-page history of Roman law written possibly in the late eleventh century. “One must know,” this text says, “that in the first beginning and genesis of Rome, when Romulus ruled, the
was without law... When the
again took power, it relied on a vague kind of law and on custom rather than functioning as a
according to the laws.” Eventually, however, they formed the committee of the Ten Men “to lay the foundations of the Roman
in the laws.”
The treatise contains some bizarre misunderstandings of early Roman history (such as that the
ruled beneath the

), but it proposes an interesting model by which the polity became lawful: no law under the kings, customary law at first in the early Republic, and proper laws later on. The second phase has theoretical affinities with Leon VI’s view of how customs can constitute a polity before receiving official ratification from him, a curious form of unofficial

such as this text proposes for the early Republic. All this, however, raises the question of the status of the lawful polity under the imperial monarchy. Unfortunately, the text is confused at this point. It claims that “in time the
grew and the number of cases and trials grew as well... And so under Caesar Augustus the divisions of the
began to pass legislation, both the commoners and the more select, along with the generals, the wise men, and the

” It is not clear what the author was thinking of here. At any rate, like most Romans he did not believe that there was any conflict between having an emperor and a lawful polity. How, then, did the Byzantines imagine that a supreme monarch could rule an
without its lapsing into a tyranny of whim? Was there not a fundamental tension between autocracy and the rule of law?

zh: 皇帝与法律：一个矛盾的化解
en: The Emperor and the Law: A Contradiction Resolved

zh: 乍看之下，乃至再看、三看，拜占庭都是一个守法政体。它拥有由合法权威颁布、编纂与修订的庞大法律体系，且无人质疑一个正当政体必须基于法律而非权贵的任意意志来治理；官员必须服从法律而非追逐私人利益；

法律应当平等而公平地适用于所有人。诚然，现实并不总是或完全符合这幅图景。个人可能违法而不受惩罚，官员可能滥用权力。我们并不真正知道法律在多大程度上被当局执行、被法庭适用、或被民众知晓。因此我们无法衡量理论与实践之间的差距。我们永远不知道拜占庭按现代社会的标准（这些标准目前正处于低潮）会如何达标。就我们的目的而言重要的是：臣民理解或希望他们的政体是一个守法政体，且法律意在既约束被统治者也约束统治者。他们对这一前提的意识与利用在早期拜占庭埃及更为明显，那里有文献证据传世。正如若埃尔·博康（Joëlle Beaucamp）所观察：
en: At first sight, as well as a second and third, Byzantium was a lawful polity. It had a substantial corpus of law that had been issued, compiled, and revised by legitimate authorities, and it was not questioned that a proper polity had to be governed on the basis of law, not the arbitrary whim of the powerful; that officials had to obey the laws and not pursue private interests;

and that the laws should be applied equally and fairly to all. To be sure, reality did not always or fully conform to this picture. It was possible for individuals to break the law and not be punished and for officials to abuse their power. We do not really know to what degree the laws were enforced by the authorities, applied in the courts, or known to the populace. We cannot then measure the gap between theory and practice. We will never know how Byzantium would measure up by the standards of modern societies (which are riding low at the moment). What matters for our purpose is that subjects understood or hoped that theirs was a lawful polity and that the laws were meant to be binding on rulers as well as the ruled. Their awareness and exploitation of this premise are more evident in early Byzantine Egypt, where documentary evidence survives. As Joëlle Beaucamp has observed:

zh: 在请求当局处理案件的请愿书及其他相关文书中，频繁提及法律。这些文本表达对法律所提供益处的总体评论……它们要求当局执行与所提交案件相关的法律……这些陈述可能仅被视为
（套语），由请愿书这一文类传统性地传递。然而，此处的“法律”一词指示一种更高的、且公共的秩序：这一秩序与当局相联系，有时明确地与皇帝相联系。
en: Mentions of the laws occur frequently in petitions and other types of documents related to proceedings before the authorities. These texts express general comments on the benefits provided by the laws... They ask the authorities to enforce the law bearing on the case submitted to them... These statements could be considered mere

traditionally conveyed by the genre of the petition. However, the term “law” here indicates a higher order, and a public one: this order is connected with the authorities and sometimes explicitly with the emperor.

zh: 是一个不容置疑的原则。如我们所见，利奥六世相信民众习惯需要正式权威（即他自己）的批准。但真正的问题、焦虑与政治反思的来源是皇帝所处的地位本身。一个政体如何能是守法的，当它由一个可以无视或取消法律、且不受法律或政治监督的皇帝治理时？这是潜伏于每个君主制中的僭主制威胁，它使西塞罗在其
）中念念不忘。
甚至在一位明智而好的国王之下也可能受到危害，“因为公共的财产（如我所说，这正是共和国的定义）取决于一人是否点头、是否愿意。”
一条细线分隔好国王与专制者。
事实上，帝国史似乎在两者之间摆动。
en: The

was an unquestioned principle. Leon VI, as we saw, believed that popular customs required ratification by formal authority (i.e., his own). But the real problem and source of anxiety and political reflection was the imperial position itself. How could a polity be lawful when it was governed by an emperor who could ignore or cancel a law and was not subject to legal or political oversight? This was the threat of tyranny that lurked in every monarchy, and it preoccupied Cicero in his
The
could be jeopardized even under a wise and good king, “for the property of the public (which is, as I said, the definition of a republic) was managed by one man’s nod and wish.”
A thin line separated good kings and despots.
In fact, imperial history seems to oscillate between the two.

zh: 关于皇帝与法律的关系已有许多讨论。我在此不感兴趣的是法律政策如何形成；法律如何颁布、解释、执行、随后编纂；或法律如何与帝国宣传相交，充当宫廷修辞的载体、并把皇帝投射为守法秩序的堡垒。我更具体指的是皇帝受制于法律还是高于法律的问题。受制于法律的皇帝近似第2章勾勒的共和国仆人模型，而存在——更重要是被认为存在——于法律之上的皇帝，至少乍看之下似乎挑战该模型。好皇帝被呈现为顺从法律权威，这要求他们某种谦逊，即便只是做样子；而坏皇帝倾向于不顾法律、为所欲为。至少这是他们的支持者与敌人分别描绘他们的方式，这表明顺从法律的皇帝模型占据道德高地、因而在意识形态上占主导。
en: There have been many discussions of the relation between the emperor and the law. I am not interested here in how legal policies were formulated; how laws were issued, interpreted, enforced, and subsequently compiled; or how law intersected with imperial propaganda, serving as a vehicle for court rhetoric and to project the emperor as a bulwark of the lawful order. I am referring more specifically to the question of whether the emperor was subject to or above the laws. An emperor who is subject to the laws would approximate the model of the servant of the republic sketched in Chapter 2, while an emperor who exists—more importantly, who is held to exist—above the laws would seem, at least at first sight, to challenge that model. Good emperors were presented as submissive to the authority of the laws, which called for a certain humility on their part, even if only a show of it, while bad emperors tended to act as they wished without regard to the law. At least this is how they were depicted by their partisans and enemies, respectively, which suggests that the model of the emperor who submits to the law held the moral high ground and, therefore, was ideologically dominant.

zh: 如上文普里斯科斯所见，皇帝像任何其他官长一样服从（或应当服从？）法律的观念，与该政体的共和前提牢固相连。但普里斯科斯在把

作为理想模型捍卫时诉诸这一原则的方式暴露了他的不安：与其说是在断言一个事实，不如说他是在提醒读者守法政体的前提条件，因为他已承认现实生活中并非一切都应然。如何确保皇帝们守法地治理？他主张的上下文使其成为纲领性的，而非必然是描述性的。但如果能让正确的人接受它，尤其是皇帝们自己，它就可能成为现实。证据表明理论家们的这些“提醒”确实传到了皇帝那里，至少在修辞层面。辛内西奥斯提出的一个定义后来成了通行说法，即合法国王使法律成为其意志，而僭主把自己的任性当成法律。
这被其他理论家逐字采纳，如六世纪的约安尼斯·吕多斯，也被皇帝采纳，如十一世纪的君士坦丁九世（Konstantinos IX），在一部设立法律学校与
（“法律守护者”）职位的
中。
该文本由约安尼斯·毛罗普斯（Ioannes Mauropous）撰写，提醒我们皇帝必须通过理论家与演说家说话。但我们不应把后者视为把其观点强加于本来不情愿的专制皇帝。皇帝们
被臣民视为守法地治理，正如他们想要被视为仅仅为臣民利益而治理（事实上我们将看到，如果他们想保住皇位、常常还有性命，他们
被如此看待）。法治政体需要依法督理。许多作家的著述与皇帝的立法，都把这视为皇帝职位的本质：它是一种
，一种守法的监督，是“全体臣民的共同善”。
en: As we saw above in Priskos, the notion that the emperor did (or should?) obey the laws just like any other magistrate was firmly linked to the republican premises of the regime. But the way Priskos invokes this principle in defending the

as an ideal model betrays his insecurity: rather than asserting a point of fact, it is more like he is reminding readers of the preconditions of a lawful polity, having acknowledged that not all is as it should be in real life. How could one ensure that emperors governed lawfully? The context of his claim makes it programmatic, and not necessarily descriptive. But if the right people could be made to accept it, especially the emperors themselves, it could became real. The evidence suggests that these “reminders” by theorists did make it through to the emperors, at least on a rhetorical level. Synesios promulgated a definition that became a commonplace, namely, that the legitimate king makes the law his will while the tyrant makes his whim the law.
This was adopted verbatim by other theorists, such as Ioannes Lydos in the sixth century, but also by emperors, such as Konstantinos IX in the eleventh, in a
establishing a school of law and the office of
(“guardian of the laws”).

The text was written by Ioannes Mauropous, reminding us that the emperors had to speak through theorists and orators. But we should not view the latter as imposing their views on otherwise reluctant authoritarian emperors. Emperors
to be seen by their subjects as governing lawfully in the same way that they wanted to be seen as governing solely in their subjects’ interests (in fact, we will see that they

to be seen this way if they wanted to keep their thrones and, often, their lives). A lawful polity had need of lawful supervision, and this is precisely what many writers and emperors in their legislation took to be the essence of the imperial position: it was an
a lawful oversight that was “a common good for all the subjects.”

zh: 429年由塞奥多西奥斯二世（Theodosios II）与瓦伦提尼安努斯三世（Valentinianus III）颁布、后来收入拜占庭
的摘要的一道敕令，走得更远，宣告了这一点：
en: An edict issued in 429 by Theodosios II and Valentinianus III, which was summarized in the Byzantine
went even further and proclaimed this:

zh: 一位在位君主宣称自己受制于法律，是配得上其威严的声明；因为我们的权威依赖于法律的权威。而主权者受制于法律是皇权最崇高的表现，且依本敕令条款，凡我们自己不得做的事，我们也禁止他人做。
en: It is a statement worthy of the majesty of a reigning prince for him to profess to be subject to the laws; for our authority is dependent upon that of the law. And it is the greatest attribute of imperial power for the sovereign to be subject to the laws, and we forbid to others what we do not suffer ourselves to do by the terms of the present edict.

zh: 不幸的是，我们缺乏这一宣告背后的上下文，它本可澄清皇帝们为何作出它。
其中确有某种好处。很可能他们收到太多豁免一般法律的请求，于是以这一宣告明示，连皇帝自己也不能享有这种豁免。现在没人能抱怨了。皇帝们干脆宣告他们像任何人一样受制于法律，并接受其地位的权威源于法律，而无人能否认这一点而不挑战
的根基本身。
en: Unfortunately, we lack the context behind this pronouncement, which would have clarified why the emperors made it.

There was certainly some advantage in it. It is likely that they were receiving too many requests for exemptions from general laws and were, with this pronouncement, ostentatiously shutting that door even for themselves. No one could complain now. The emperors simply proclaimed that they were as subject to the laws as anyone else and accepted that the authority of their position stemmed from the law, which no one could deny without challenging the very foundations of the

zh: 如果我们到此为止，拜占庭政体在性质上是共和的这一观点将获得又一根支持支柱。皇帝们宣称他们受制于非人格的公共制度，不亚于其臣民。事实上，无论我们可能遇到什么替代或相反的证据，我们在此已有足够材料得出结论：至少存在一种相信共和式君主制的意愿。
en: If we left matters there, the view that the Byzantine polity was republican in nature would gain another pillar of support. The emperors professed that they were subject to impersonal public institutions no less than were their subjects. In fact, no matter what alternative or rival evidence we might encounter, we have enough here to conclude that there was at least a will to believe in a republican monarchy.

zh: 但当从另一观点看此事时，也可能得出皇帝事实上高于法律的结论，导致关于皇帝地位的法律理论中的根本张力。这在现代学术中引起了矛盾的讨论，在两种观点之间摆动。我将先解释皇帝高于法律这一观点的理由，然后论证两种观点尽管存在张力，最终是可调和的——但仅当我们接受
的优先性与至上性。没有它，罗马关于皇帝的观点就是矛盾的，使现代学者别无选择只能接受更犬儒、更专制的观点（以免显得是理想主义者）。
en: But when the matter was looked at from a different point of view, it was possible to conclude that the emperor in fact stood above the law, leading to a fundamental tension in legal theory about the imperial position. This has caused a conflicted discussion in modern scholarship, which oscillates between the two views. I will first explain the rationale for the view that the emperor stood above the law and then argue that the two views, for all that they were in tension, were ultimately reconcilable—but only if we accept the priority and supremacy of the
Without that, the Roman view of the emperor is contradictory, leaving modern scholars no choice but to accept the more cynical, authoritarian view (lest they appear to be idealists).

zh: 皇帝是最高立法权威，也是最高上诉法院。他可以修改法律，如果他认为那样对政体最好；事实上，当现行法律不再服务政体需要时，他有责任如此做。查士丁尼
承认法律必须不断适应变化的情势，即
（事物的多变本性），
这也是三个半世纪后利奥六世
背后的前提。我们在第1章看到利奥批准与废止法律，就像他擢升官员或让官员退职一样。此外，正如法律理论早已理解的，法律在面对以独特情势为前提的特定案件时往往过于一般与僵化。必须以正义之名作出例外，但这些只能由当时办理案件的人裁量。
法律出自皇帝，那么他如何能受制于它？这种张力在希腊理论中催生了国王作为“活的”或“有生命的”法律（ἔμψυχος νόμος）的观念，一个活的、行走的、说话的法律渊源。这一概念被许多拜占庭皇帝援引，尽管他们在每次场合究竟意指什么并不透明。
在一篇公开演说中，君士坦提乌斯二世（Constantius II）与塞奥多西奥斯一世（Theodosius I）的宣传家塞米斯提奥斯（Themistios）从这一概念推导出皇帝高于法律。
而我们在
）中发现“
（元首）不受法律约束”的意见（被带入
此外，一些历史学家论证，维持一定程度的法律含混符合皇帝们的利益，以便主张他们作为最终仲裁者的相关性与权威。
en: The emperor was the supreme legislative authority and also the highest court of appeal. He could alter the law if he thought that was best for the polity; in fact, he had a responsibility to do so when current law no longer served the polity’s needs. Justinian’s
recognize that the laws have to be continually adapted to changing circumstances, the
and this was also the premise behind the

of Leon VI three and half centuries later. We saw in Chapter 1 that Leon ratified and annulled laws just as if he were promoting and retiring magistrates. Moreover, as legal theory had long understood, laws are often too general and inflexible when it comes to particular cases premised on unique circumstances. Exceptions had to be made in the name of justice, but these could be made only by the judgment of men acting in real time.

Law emanated from the emperor, so how could he be subject to it? This tension gave rise in Greek theory to the idea of the king as a “living” or “animate” law (ἔμψυχος νόμος), a living, walking, and speaking source of law. This concept was invoked by many Byzantine emperors, though what exactly they meant by it on each occasion is opaque.
In a public oration, Themistios, a propagandist for Constantius II and Theodosius I, deduced from this concept that emperors were above the laws.
And we find the opinion in the
that “the
is not bound by the laws” (carried over into the
Moreover, some historians have argued that it served the emperors’ interests to maintain a level of legal ambiguity in order to assert their relevance and authority as ultimate arbiters.

zh: 统治权威可以为在特定实例中服务更高目的、或防止不寻常案件扭曲一般规则之精神而对给定规则作出例外的观念，在拜占庭被称为
（权变）。它是一个需要审慎管理、更高正义感、道德共识以及务实主义、并承认并非所有目的都能同时服务的选项。
最常在教会法适用中被援引，但本身是一个宽泛概念。上帝对历史的干预也被看作这种意义上的权宜处置，且行省法官不被期望在所有案件中字面而严格地适用法律。
在其一部
中，利奥六世指出皇帝可以“施行 οἰκονομία，但这并不违反法律。因为那些被上帝托付管理（οἰκονομία）世俗事务的人，被允许在高于治理臣民之法律的层面上管理它们（οἰκονομεῖν）。”
十二世纪，当教会法学家塞奥多罗斯·巴尔萨蒙（Theodoros Balsamon）指出“皇帝不受法律或教规约束”时，他援引了“帝国
”的特权。
en: The idea that a governing authority could make an exception to a given rule in order to serve a higher purpose in a specific instance or to prevent an unusual case from warping the spirit of the general rule was called

in Byzantium. It was an option that called for prudent management, a higher sense of justice, and moral consensus as well as pragmatism and an acknowledgment that not all ends could be served at once.

was invoked most commonly in the application of canon law but was, in itself, a broad concept. God’s interventions in history were regarded as “economical” in this sense, and provincial judges were not expected to literally and strictly apply the law in all cases.
In one of his

Leon VI noted that an emperor can “practice οἰκονομία, but this is not contrary to the law. For those who are entrusted by God with the management (οἰκονομία) of worldly affairs are permitted to manage them (οἰκονομεῖν) at a level above the law that governs subjects.”
In the twelfth century, when the canonist Theodoros Balsamon noted that “the emperor is not subject to the laws or to the canons,” he cited the prerogative of “imperial

zh: 鉴于没有更高的法律权威，正如
所言，“令
喜悦者具有法律效力。”
中的希腊译文走得更远，说“令
喜悦者即是法律。”
这必然适用，无论皇帝是颁布正式的一般法律、在特定案件中作出法律裁决、书面授予豁免、还是干脆口头命令其官员或臣民做某事。这种含混使他们招致批评。例如阿米安努斯抱怨，恺撒伽卢斯（Caesar Gallus）所说的任何话都具有法律效力。这使他成为僭主。
但同样的效果也可通过书面立法达到，正如普罗科匹乌斯抱怨查士丁尼那样。查士丁尼比其他皇帝更常通过颁布法律来施政，在法条中交代并具体规定他要求怎样做。
尽管许多证据已散佚，似乎后来的皇帝以不同方式颁布命令来治理。
那些命令即使不是正式法律也具有“法律效力”。但如果皇帝的意志就是法律，那么问他高于法律还是受制于法律就几乎没有意义。我们时期只有一位皇帝（尼基弗鲁斯三世·博塔内亚特斯）通过了一部主要意在适用于其他皇帝的法律。据我们所知它从未被执行，且确实没有开创趋势。
en: Given that there was no higher legal authority, as the
put it, “what pleases the
has the force of law.”
The Greek translation in the
went further in saying that “what pleases the
is a law.”

This necessarily applied whether the emperor issued a formal general law, made a legal decision in a particular case, granted an exemption in writing, or simply verbally ordered one of his officials or subjects to do something. This ambiguity opened them to criticism. Ammianus, for example, complained that whatever the Caesar Gallus said held the force of law. This made him a tyrant.

But the same effect could be achieved through written legislation, as Prokopios complained about Justinian. It was he who, more than any other emperor, governed by issuing laws that explained and specified what he wanted done.
Though much evidence has been lost, it seems that later emperors governed by issuing orders in different ways.

Those orders had “the force of law” even if they were not formally laws. But if the emperor’s will was the law, it makes little sense to ask whether he was above the law or subject to it. Only one emperor in our period (Nikephoros III Botaneiates) passed a law that was meant to apply primarily to other emperors. It was never enforced, as far as we know, and certainly did not set a trend.

zh: 因此史料是矛盾的。皇帝受制于法律还是高于法律？他的权威基于法律还是相反？罗马人没有设计任何法律学说来解决这个难题。
皇帝、理论家与臣民所做的反而是用一个公式突破它，该公式本质上是共和意志的表达，将在拜占庭法律传统中回响：“虽然我们不受法律约束，但我们仍然遵守它们。”
皇帝们在作出个人承诺：自愿遵守法律，尽管他们有可以不如此做的选项。这把共和国仆人与“有生命的法律”结合起来，并解释了那些对特定法律过度服从的著名行为，如图拉真（Trajan）与尤利安（Julian）所为。
正如查尔斯·帕兹德尼克（Charles Pazdernik）所观察：
en: The sources, therefore, are contradictory. Was the emperor subject to the law or above the laws? Was his authority grounded in law or the reverse? The Romans devised no legal doctrine to solve this conundrum.

What emperors, theorists, and subjects did instead was break through it with a formula that was essentially an expression of republican will that would echo in the Byzantine legal tradition: “While we are not bound by the laws, still we abide by them.”

The emperors were making a personal pledge to voluntarily abide by the laws even though they had the option of not doing so. This combined the republican servant with the “animate law” and explained celebrated acts of extravagant obedience to specific laws, such as by Trajan and Julian.
As Charles Pazdernik has observed:

zh: 罗马帝国意识形态从未否定这一原则：好皇帝不应显得高于法律，且不应做任何违反法律之事；一位未能表现出对其在国家中角色之正确理解的皇帝，可能被扣上僭主的帽子，这样一来，起而反抗他就可能有了正当理由，僭主之名也可能成为历史对他的最终判词。尽管遵守这些约束在很大程度上是礼仪与帝国自我呈现方式的问题，是政治剧场的一部分而非对权力不可逾越的限制，皇帝们充分理解维护对法律的尊重与守法表象的价值，将其作为其权威的关键支撑。
en: Roman imperial ideology never repudiated the principle that a good emperor should not appear to be above the law and that he should do nothing contrary to the laws; an emperor who failed to evince a correct understanding of his role within the state was susceptible of being branded a tyrant, an outcome that might not only authorize insurrection but also represent the settled judgment of history. Although the observance of such strictures was in large measure a matter of decorum and modes of imperial self-presentation, part of political theater rather than an insurmountable limitation on power, emperors well understood the value of conserving respect for the law and appearance of lawfulness as a critical underpinning of their authority.

zh: 我们将在第4、5章研究当皇帝未能把握正确基调时那些叛乱可能采取的形式。
en: We will study the form that those insurrections could take, when emperors failed to strike the right tone, in Chapters 4 and 5.

zh: 一定量的剧场是由该政体的共和基础所强加的。但帝国守法不只是表象问题，因为法律秩序的完整性必须维持，皇帝才能根本治理，正如牧首尼古拉奥斯（Nikolaos）所指出的。
过多干预可能破坏整个体制，尽管干预同样可能或更可能源自寻求恩惠的臣民而非帝国意志。491年，阿纳斯塔修斯指示其法官不接受“任何违反一般法律或有损公共利益的批复、特敕或皇帝批示
……也不要犹豫在各方面遵循一般帝国宪令。”
实质上，皇帝是在主张一般法律相对于他或其前任可能在个别案件中通过的特定法令的道德与法律至上性。这意在保护
的完整性，免受那些为一己之目的扭曲帝国权力的臣民之害。1158年，曼努埃尔一世颁布了类似指令。
皇帝们依赖其法律顾问把他们保持在先例与合法性的界限内，
且至少有一个案例（十一世纪）中一位高等法院法官拒绝了皇帝对一部法律的理解，讽刺地解释说：
皇帝只是在对该事行使立法权，那么他的决定当然必须成立；但
它是基于那部既存法律而提出的，那么“陛下神圣的尊威有义务真正了解相关法律”（据斯皮罗斯·特罗亚诺斯（Spyros Troianos），该法官“让皇帝明白了自己的分寸”）。
en: A certain amount of theater was imposed by the republican foundations of the regime. But imperial lawabidingness was not only a matter of appearance, for the integrity of the legal order had to be maintained for emperors to govern at all, as the patriarch Nikolaos noted.

Too much interference could undermine the entire system, though interference was as likely or more to originate from subjects seeking favors as from the imperial will. In 491, Anastasios instructed his judges not to accept “any rescript, pragmatic sanction, or imperial notation that is contrary to the general law or adverse to the public interest
... nor to hesitate to follow in every respect the general imperial constitutions.”

In effect, the emperor was asserting the moral and legal supremacy of general laws over specific enactments that he or his predecessors might have passed in individual cases. This was meant to protect the integrity of the
against subjects who would twist imperial power for their own ends. In 1158, Manuel I issued a similar directive.
Emperors relied on their legal advisors to keep them within the bounds of precedent and legality,
and there is at least one case (from the eleventh century) where a high court judge rejected an emperor’s understanding of a law, explaining sarcastically that
the emperor were simply exercising his legislative power in the matter, then his decision must stand, of course, but

it were being offered on the basis of that existing law, then “your holy Majesty has an obligation to actually know the law in question” (according to Spyros Troianos, the judge “put him in his place”).

zh: 因此罗马法律传统仍然是与帝国意志分离的某种东西，且大部分独立于君主运作，有时甚至制衡他。
更重要是，权力除非被视为守法否则不被认为合法。达格龙（Dagron）敏锐地指出：“权力本身不具正当性。不过，夺得权力的人若选择尊重法律，便能取得正当性……统治者转而依法行事，才获得了正当性。”
此外，在反驳皇帝是帝国全部土地所有者这一观念时，G. C. 马尼亚蒂斯（G. C. Maniatis）论证“拜占庭历史学家认为没收是对财产所有者权利的侵犯，而非皇帝合法权利的行使。”非法没收可能罕见，但它们确实凸显了滥用的潜在可能。
“拜占庭中期的正义观念，”安格利基·拉伊乌（Angeliki Laiou）在一篇论经济意识形态的论文中解释，“包括这样一种关切：所有臣民（尤其较弱者）的财产应受保护，一个正当而有序的社会不应因对他人权利与财产的侵犯而被扰乱。”
臣民与皇帝都同意
必须是
的，而这一共识在如此程度上约束并塑造了每个人的行动与期望，以致皇帝例行地宣告他们自己将遵守法律，尽管他们并无必要如此。
en: The Roman legal tradition, therefore, remained something separate from the imperial will and operated, for the most part, independently of the monarch and sometimes even to check him.

More importantly, power was not taken to be legitimate unless it was perceived to be lawful. Dagron has astutely pointed out that “it was not power that was legitimate; but whoever appropriated power could be made legitimate by choosing to respect the law... Legitimacy was achieved through a conversion to legality.”

Also, in refuting the notion that the emperor was the owner of all land in the empire, G. C. Maniatis argues that “Byzantine historians held that confiscations were an infringement on the rights of property owners and not an exercise of the emperor’s lawful rights.” Illegal confiscations were probably rare, but they do highlight a potential for abuse.

“The middle Byzantine idea of justice,” Angeliki Laiou explained in a paper on economic ideology, “included the concern that the possessions of all subjects (especially the weaker ones) should be safeguarded and that a proper and orderly society should not be disturbed by encroachment on the rights and possessions of others.”
Both subjects and emperors agreed that the
had to be

and this consensus constrained and shaped everyone’s actions and expectations to such a degree that emperors routinely declared that they would abide by the laws themselves even though they did not have to.

zh: 从实践观点看，这一解决或妥协并不像乍看那样糟，尤其如果我们把皇帝在其统治被视为无法无天时可能遭受的极端惩罚考虑在内。但从法律观点看，这一状况在该领域导致了某种僵局。拜占庭人是否对法律权威与帝国权力之间的关系如此根本地困惑，以致只能诉诸共和传统下的自愿承诺来破局？权衡正反史料然后宣告拜占庭人“总体上”相信皇帝受制于法律，是不够的。
他们并非在两种矛盾的帝国权力观（其一共和、其一专制）之间挣扎。两种观点事实上互补，但显得矛盾，因为我们把这个问题作为一个技术法律问题来考察，而没有考虑首先框架该问题的政体的更宽上下文。正是当我们把
排除在考察之外（如大多数学术所做），皇帝才被留在辉煌的孤立中，带来我们所见的问题性结果。于是我们面对人为的挑战：拼凑矛盾的宣告、权衡其相对价值或频率，试图发现哪一个是真的、或大部分时间是真的、或“总体上”是真的，或寻找一个解决基本问题的公式：皇帝是法律权威的渊源还是相反？要逃离这一两难，我们必须把皇帝在法律中的地位问题（次要的）转换为他在政体中的地位问题（首要的）。
en: From a practical point of view, this solution or compromise is not as bad as it might seem at first, especially if we factor in the extreme punishments that emperors could suffer if their rule was perceived as lawless. But from the legal point of view this situation has led to something of an impasse in the field. Were the Byzantines so fundamentally confused about the relationship between legal authority and imperial power that they could break the stalemate only through an act of republican will? It is insufficient to weigh the sources for and against and declare that “overall” the Byzantines believed that emperors were subject to the law.

They were not struggling with two contradictory views of imperial power, the one republican and the other despotic. The two views were in fact complementary but appear to be contradictory because we have examined this issue as a technical legal question without considering the broader context of the polity that framed the issue in the first place. It is when we remove the

from the equation, as most scholarship does, that the emperor is left in splendid isolation, with the problematic results that we have seen. We are then faced with the artificial challenge of assembling contradictory pronouncements and weighing their relative value or frequency in an attempt to discover which one was true, or true most of the time, or “overall,” or to look for a formula that resolves the basic problem: was the emperor the source of the law’s authority or the reverse? To escape from this dilemma, then, we have to convert the question of the emperor’s standing in the law, which was secondary, to the question of his standing in the polity, which was primary.

zh: 终极标准不是法律本身，而是共和国的公共善：
（共和国的安康是最高法律）。
皇帝的工作是促进它，而法律是表达该善并保护它免受私人利益侵害的工具。关于某事的特定法律不能提供最终标准：它们只是保护共同价值的临时调节机制。同样的原则也治理教会法的执行。
终极标准是皇帝们所称的“全体的益处”之类，或西塞罗在其
定义中所称的
（因共享利益而结合）。
en: The ultimate standard was not the law itself but the common good of the republic:

The emperor’s job was to promote it and the law was an instrument that expressed that good and protected it from private interests. Particular laws on a matter could not provide the final standard: they were only temporary regulatory mechanisms to protect common values. The same principle governed the enforcement of ecclesiastical law too.
The ultimate standard was what emperors called “the benefit of all” or the like, or what Cicero had called, in his definition of the
a

zh: 皇帝不受法律约束的法律学说由
（授权法）演化而来，在罗马帝国存在的前三个世纪，它正式授权每位皇帝统治。P. A. 布伦特（P. A. Brunt）识别出唯一传世的此类
（韦斯巴芗（Vespasian）的那部）中最终催生我们所讨论学说的条款：“凡[皇帝]认为符合
的利益以及神、人、公共与私人利益之尊严者，他应有权力与权利去做与执行。”
总之，皇帝有义务服从法律，除非公共善要求他不如此：一般情形与这一例外相辅相成。例如在一般意义上，君士坦丁与李锡尼（Licinius）宣告正义与公平应优先于法律的严格字面。
en: The legal doctrine that the emperor was not bound by the laws evolved out of the
which, for the first three centuries of the Roman empire’s existence, formally authorized each emperor to rule. P. A. Brunt identified the clause in the only surviving such
(that of Vespasian), which eventually gave rise to the doctrine we are discussing: “Whatever [the emperor] considers to be in accordance with the advantage of the
and the dignity of divine, human, public, and private interests he shall have the right and the power to do and to execute.”

In sum, the emperor was bound to obey the laws unless the common good required him not to: these contingencies were complementary. In a general sense, for example, Constantine and Licinius declared that justice and fairness should prevail over the strict letter of the law.

zh: 一部法律可能变得不利或过时，而太多法律可能造成混乱。这些我们在利奥六世
中已看到，他相信自己通过改革在恢复与改进
。单纯合法性不等同于公共善。这一点例如在普罗科匹乌斯
中清楚显现，它以查士丁尼毁掉罗马政体为由谴责他为僭主。然而查士丁尼并非总是非法行动：他的许多罪行有适当的临时法律支撑。
他的统治在许多方面是一种合乎法条的僭政，但普罗科匹乌斯是以更高标准评判皇帝及其法律的：
的善。此外——这是关键一点——

children: 在罗马与拜占庭传统中，从未接受过皇帝可以为造福罗马人民以外的任何理由而行动于法律之外的观点。

zh: 换言之，压倒性标准不是成文法的标准；它是共和国的善。成文法与皇帝的法外行为都由该标准评判。其一并不总是优于另一：成文法可能是坏法律，而技术上非法的帝国行为可能因其正义而获普遍赞扬。在此意义上，法律与皇帝同样是共和国的仆人，分别是固定的与“有生命的”正义渊源，并被期望为全体罗马人的善协同工作。阿拉伯哲学家伊本·鲁世德（Ibn Rushd，阿威罗伊 Averroes）据此“区分了依固定而不可变法律统治的城市（如伊斯兰法的情形）与法律随着当下最合宜的做法而改变的城市（如拜占庭许多法律的情形）。”
en: A law could become disadvantageous or obsolete, and too many laws could create confusion. This much we saw in the
of Leon VI, who believed he was restoring and improving the
through his reforms. Mere legality was not equivalent to the public good. This emerges clearly, for example, in Prokopios’s
which denounces Justinian as a tyrant on the grounds that he ruined the Roman polity. Yet Justinian was not always acting illegally: many of his crimes were backed up with an appropriate ad hoc law.
His was in many ways a lawful tyranny, but Prokopios was judging the emperor and his laws by a higher standard: the good of the
Moreover, and this is the crucial point,

children: never in the Roman and Byzantine tradition was the view accepted that the emperor could act beyond the law for any reason other than to benefit the Roman people.

en: In other words, the overriding criterion was not that of the written law; it was the good of the republic. Both the written law and the extralegal acts of the emperors were evaluated by that standard. The one was not always better than the other: a written law could be a bad law, whereas a technically illegal imperial act could be universally praised for its justice. In this sense, both the law and the emperor were equally servants of the republic, being a fixed and an “animate” source of justice, respectively, and expected to work together for the good of all Romans. The Arab philosopher Ibn Rushd (Averroes) accordingly “distinguished between cities that are ruled according to fixed and immutable laws, as is the case with the Islamic law, and cities whose laws change according to what is most expedient, as is the case with many of the laws in Byzantium.”

zh: 我们将看到，此类法外行为的动机与情势受公共舆论密切关注与评判。正如哈里斯（Harries）所论证，“共识排除了统治者的任意决定。”
也许它与其说排除它们，不如说使它们极其危险。臣民有时必须行使独立道德判断，评判帝国命令应否被遵循。当我们转向拜占庭政治行动的共和面向时，将考察这种“抵抗权”的案例。目前指出基本原则已被理解应已足够。凯考梅诺斯（Kekaumenos），十一世纪晚期一位谦逊但绝非不聪明的作家，承认：
en: The motives and circumstances of such extralegal actions, we will see, were closely watched and evaluated by public opinion. As Harries has argued, “consensus precluded arbitrary decisions by the ruler.”

Perhaps it did not so much preclude them as make them extremely risky. Subjects sometimes had to exercise independent moral judgment and evaluate whether imperial orders should be followed or not. We will examine cases of this “right to resistance” when we turn to the republican dimensions of political action in Byzantium. For now it should suffice to point out that the basic principle was understood. Kekaumenos, a modest but hardly unintelligent writer of the late eleventh century, acknowledged that:

zh: “有人说皇帝不受法律约束、而是法律，我也这么说。在他所做与所立法的一切中他做得好，我们应服从他；但如果他说“喝毒药”，绝不要做。如果他说“跳进海里游过去”，也不要这样做。由此须知皇帝是人，且受宗教的法律约束。”
en: some say that the emperor is not subject to the law, but is a law, and I say this too. In all that he does and legislates he does well and we should obey him, but if he should say, “drink poison,” by no means do it. If he says, “jump in the sea and swim across it,” don’t do this either. So know from this that the emperor is a man and is subject to the laws of religion.

zh: 宗教当然是拜占庭人公共善构想的一个基本要素，尽管凯考梅诺斯的两个例子都不特定是宗教的，更不源自某一特定宗教。他的“宗教的法律”指向一种模糊的自然法构想。宗教争论本身也催生了抵抗帝国意志的理论，但它们所催生的原则再次基于一般道德考量。见证十世纪早期一位被废牧首尼古拉奥斯致教宗的信，谈他如何个人恳求利奥六世不要娶第四位妻子：
en: Religion was, of course, an essential element of the Byzantines’ conception of the common good, though neither of Kekaumenos’s examples is specifically religious, far less stems from a particular religion. His “laws of religion” point to a vague conception of natural law. Religious controversies proper also occasioned theories of resistance to the imperial will, but the principles to which they gave rise were, again, based on general moral considerations. Witness Nikolaos, a deposed patriarch in the early tenth century, writing to the pope about how he personally pleaded with Leon VI not to take a fourth wife:

zh: “人们说，皇帝是未成文的法律”，并非为了让他可以打破法律、为所欲为，而是为了让他在法律没有明文授权的情况下，其所作所为也应合于成文法所体现的原则。
en: “The emperor,” they say, “is an unwritten law,” not so that he may break laws and do whatever he pleases, but so that he may be such in his unauthorized actions as a written law would be.

zh: 也就是说，无论在遵循还是不遵循既存法律时，皇帝都应以其臣民的善为目标，以维持
。在同一封信的后文，尼古拉奥斯发展出一种抵抗理论：
en: That is, in both following and not following existing law, the emperor ought to be aiming at the good of his subjects in sustaining the
Later in the same letter, Nikolaos develops a theory of resistance:

zh: 皇帝的尊位固然重大，服从皇帝、不抵抗其敕令是对的，但仅对那些显示帝国统治之尊严的敕令如此。他命令我们行正义吗？这些是真正的帝国敕令，对这些我们绝不可抵抗。皇帝命令我们拿起武器对抗敌人吗？他决定我们必须为公共利益（τὴν τῶν κοινῶν λυσιτέλειαν）贡献某种东西吗？那么就应当欣然听从他的决定。他命令我们做其他任何可能为其统治与其臣民带来力量与荣誉之事吗？那么我们必须立刻照办。这些是皇帝的职责……另一方面，他……命令我们放弃对上帝的虔诚吗？但这不是皇帝的职责：因此我们绝不可服从，必须无视其命令，视之为一个不虔诚之人的不虔诚敕令。他命令我们诽谤、以诡计杀害他人、败坏他人婚姻、或非法夺取他人财物吗？然而这不是帝国政府的行为，而是拦路贼、诽谤者、通奸者、窃贼的行为……说“因为他是皇帝”就允许他以无人会允许其臣民的方式犯罪，这是邪恶的、是最邪恶的学说。
en: The imperial dignity is indeed a great matter, and it is right to obey emperors and not to resist their edicts, but only in those edicts that display the dignity of the imperial rule. Does he order us to do justly? These are truly imperial edicts, and these we must not resist. Does the emperor order us to take arms against the enemy? Does he decide that we must contribute something to the public interest (τὴν τῶν κοινῶν λυσιτέλειαν)? His decision must then be obeyed eagerly. Does he order us to do whatever else may bring strength and honor to his rule and to his subjects? We must then do his bidding at once. These things are the emperor’s duties... On the other hand, does he... bid us renounce our piety toward God? But this is not an emperor’s duty: so that we must not obey, and must ignore his order as the impious edict of an impious man. Does he bid us to slander, to slay another by guile, to corrupt another’s marriage, or wrongfully take another’s goods? This, however, is not a work of an imperial government, but rather of a footpad, a slanderer, an adulterer, a thief... It is evil, it is most evil doctrine to say that “because he is an emperor” he is permitted to sin in a way that no one would permit his subjects to do.

zh: 拜占庭史充满拒绝服从皇帝命令的男女实例，多基于宗教理由。
en: Byzantine history abounds in instances of men and women who refused to obey an emperor’s orders, mostly on religious grounds.

zh: 在考虑法外帝国行为时，我们不应只停留于其负面面向、即任意“僭主式”行为。法外干预可以因尼古拉奥斯所引的正面理由而被证成，且他所列项目可被用来反对他的特定立场。例如利奥六世可以论证其第四次婚姻满足这些条件之一，如“为公共利益贡献某种东西”，也许通过确保王朝稳定与合法性。这里有分歧的空间，因此有政治与缔造共识的斗争。但无论哪种方式皇帝都必须在臣民面前陈述理由。一位母亲向尤利安抱怨他只流放而未处决强奸其女儿的人。尤利安诉诸更高法律：“法律可能责备我的仁慈，但一位仁慈的皇帝可以高于其他法律。”
塞奥多罗斯·斯图迪特斯（Theodoros the Stoudite）激烈反对君士坦丁六世（Konstantinos VI）的一次婚姻，他声称那不是
而是
——纯粹非法。
不合常规的婚姻在十一世纪再次受到批评，
且1043年人民（ὁ δῆμος =
）在一次游行队列中奋起，威胁要杀死皇帝，因为他们相信他意图娶其情妇。
人民对这些事有意见，或可被说服而产生意见。
en: In considering extralegal imperial acts, we should not dwell only on their negative aspect, on arbitrary “tyrannical” acts. Extralegal interventions could be justified for the positive reasons cited by Nikolaos, and the items that he lists could be used against his specific position. For instance, Leon VI could argue that his fourth marriage fulfilled one of these conditions, such as “contributing something to the public interest,” perhaps by ensuring dynastic stability and legitimacy. There was room for disagreement here and therefore for politics and the struggle to build consensus. But either way emperors had to make the case before their subjects. A mother complained to Julian that he had only banished and not executed the rapist of her daughter. Julian appealed to a higher law: “The laws may reproach my clemency, but a merciful emperor may rise above other laws.”
Theodoros the Stoudite argued vehemently against a marriage of Konstantinos VI that, he claimed, was not
but
—just illegality.
Irregular unions were criticized again in the eleventh century,
and in 1043 the people (ὁ δῆμος =
) rose up and threatened to kill the emperor during a procession in the belief that he intended to marry his mistress.
The people had opinions about these matters, or could be persuaded to have them.

zh: 总之，合法性（legality）不如正当性（legitimacy）重要，而当皇帝培育他们为全体罗马人利益治理的观感时，正当性得以维持。做到这一点的一种方式、且可能最容易的方式，是实际为全体罗马人利益治理。归根结底，正当性是唯一重要的事，而正当性我们将看到意味着受欢迎。是否遵守法律是次要的，但它可能也是最安全的。
en: In sum, legality was not as important as legitimacy, and legitimacy was maintained when emperors cultivated the perception that they were governing in the interests of all the Romans. One way to do this, and probably the easiest, was to actually govern in the interests of all the Romans. Ultimately, legitimacy was the only thing that mattered, and legitimacy, we will see, meant popularity. Whether one adhered to the law was secondary, but it was probably safest too.

zh: 法外权威总是一场赌博。普塞洛斯说巴西尔二世（Basileios II）不依照法律，而是按自己的判断统治，但普塞洛斯认可其结果，且似乎大多数拜占庭人也如此。
另一方面，米海尔三世（Michael III）在其被杀后被其凶手巴西尔一世的后代妖魔化。案件事实可能非我们所能触及，但批评被表述的方式表明其作者与受众（包括一位皇帝君士坦丁七世）如何理解皇帝与共和国规范之间的关系。米海尔据说从事各种卑劣行为、且不经正当审判仅凭意志处死人。
总之，他冒犯了“宗教顾忌与
的法律及自然的法律”。
“他以一种与该
之规范本身相反的方式行为并参与
因此米海尔因其违规而被杀，或这些文本要我们相信如此。这把我们带到皇帝最初如何在政体内被制衡的问题，我指实践层面，该讨论我留到第4章。
en: Extralegal authority was always a gamble. Psellos says that Basileios II ruled not according to the laws but to the dictates of his own mind, yet Psellos approved the results, and so, it seems, did most Byzantines.

Michael III, on the other hand, was demonized after his murder by the descendants of his killer, Basileios I. The facts of the case may be beyond our reach, but the way in which the criticisms were couched indicates how their authors and audience, including an emperor (Konstantinos VII), understood the relationship between the emperor and the norms of the republic. Michael is said to have engaged in various vile practices and to have put people to death without proper trials, simply on a whim.
In sum, he offended against “religious scruples and against the laws of the
and those of nature.”
“He was behaving and taking part in the
in a way that was opposite to the very norms of that

Michael was therefore killed for his infractions, or so these texts would have us believe. This brings us to the question of how the emperor was kept in check within the polity in the first place, I mean in practical terms, a discussion I will defer to Chapter 4.

zh: 在结束本节时，我想呈现两位拜占庭法律学者如何理论化或想象皇帝的非法或法外行为。十三世纪早期，奥赫里德主教德米特里奥斯·科马特诺斯（Demetrios Chomatenos）认为，塞奥多罗斯·拉斯卡里斯（Theodoros Laskaris）不经审判处决一名强盗并非罪过，只要它是“为促进公共善（ὑπὲρ ὠφελείας τοῦ κοινοῦ）”而做。
但赦免也可能是“非法的”。在其

中，身为高级法官的阿塔莱亚特斯（Attaleiates）呈现一个关于诺曼雇佣兵鲁塞利奥斯（Rouselios）的情景，后者已在对抗席卷小亚细亚的突厥人时证明了自己的本领，但随后反叛了皇帝。依法律鲁塞利奥斯必须被定罪，但帝国利益要求把他派出去对抗突厥人。阿塔莱亚特斯设计了一个理论情景，使皇帝能够兼顾两方面，结合合法性与法外帝国干预。以下是他设想此事如何展开（最终并未发生，但这让我们看到一位拜占庭法官如何
帝国权威在严格法律字面之外的干预）：
en: In closing this section, I would like to present how two Byzantine legal scholars theorized or imagined illegal or extralegal behavior by emperors. In the early thirteenth century, the bishop of Ohrid Demetrios Chomatenos opined that it was no sin on the part of Theodoros Laskaris to have executed a robber without trial so long as it was done “for the promotion of the common good (ὑπὲρ ὠφελείας τοῦ κοινοῦ).”
But pardons too could be “illegal.” In his

Attaleiates, a high-ranking judge, presents a scenario regarding the Norman mercenary Rouselios who had proven his mettle against the Turks overrunning Asia Minor but who had then rebelled against the emperor. By law, Rouselios had to be condemned, but the interests of the empire called for him to be sent out against the Turks. Attaleiates devised a theoretical scenario that allowed him to have it both ways, combining legality and extralegal imperial intervention. Here is how he thought this could play out (it did not happen in the end, but that allows us to see how a Byzantine judge
the intervention of imperial authority outside the strict letter of the law):

zh: 皇帝无意把俘虏带来亲自见一见，也未作出配得上帝国仁慈与宽宏的决定——那本会是对其提起法律诉讼、在裁决达成后判处其死刑，所有这些都是为了能够在那时以温和与怜悯调和其正义的愤怒，从而为罗马帝国保留一位如此级别的士兵与指挥官，他能够医治东方许多化脓的伤口。如此一来，鲁塞利奥斯会对皇帝饶他一命深表感激，并表达无尽的谢意。
en: The emperor had no intention to bring the captive before his presence and into his sight, nor did he reach a decision worthy of imperial benevolence and magnanimity, which would have been to bring legal proceedings against him, and, after the verdict had been reached, to condemn him to death, all in order to be able, at that point, to temper his righteous wrath with gentleness and compassion and thus to preserve for the Roman empire a soldier and commander of his caliber, who was capable of healing many of the wounds festering in the east. Thus the latter would admit an immense gratitude towards the emperor for his salvation and express endless thanks.

zh: 阿塔莱亚特斯的理想是严格合法性、辅以为了公共善作出例外的能力。这是大多数拜占庭人看待其皇帝非凡权力与地位的方式，且他们保留评判他使用这些权力之好坏的权利。皇帝与法律的关系不是一个法律问题；它是一个政治问题，须以政治方式处理。但政体如何能对其皇帝强制执行其规范与其裁决？
en: Attaleiates’s ideal was strict legality tempered by the ability to make exceptions for the common good. This was how most Byzantines viewed the extraordinary powers and position of their emperor, and they reserved the right to judge him on how well he used those powers. The emperor’s relationship to the law was not a legal question; it was a political one, to be dealt with politically. But how could the polity enforce its norms, and its verdicts, on the emperor?

zh: 他律中的自主
en: Autonomy in Heteronomy

zh: 在其关于早期帕列奥列格时期史料中皇帝与法律动态的讨论中，迪米特尔·安格洛夫（Dimiter Angelov）指出，颂词演说倾向于宣告皇帝高于法律，而其他文类的作品（有时出自同一作者）则解释法外行为要取得正当性所须满足的严格条件，例如践行公认美德如仁爱，以及臣民权利不应被侵犯。
这种文类间的分工是有道理的，因为颂词的目的是突出皇帝个人美德，而这在道德自主的行为中被鲜明展示。相比之下，君主之镜倾向于把皇帝呈现为一个仅仅的职位持有者，应当服从法律。
服从法律本身是一个值得赞扬的选择，对应于守法与（共和式）谦逊的帝国美德。因此也可能引用采取那种进路的颂词演说，从普林尼（Pliny）论图拉真开始，到十三世纪仍然强劲。

我们迄今赖以重构拜占庭共和国参数的不同文类反映单一底层意识形态，在每种文类中以不同方式变调：法律史料呈现帝国职位的职能，正如皇帝希望其臣民感知它们那样；颂词演说旨在证明每位皇位占据者个人适合该职位；君主之镜是自我反思的外化形式，皇帝借此承认其职责、认清王权与僭主制之别；而史学是每位皇帝被其他文类所宣告标准评判的文类。宗教论证与修辞在所有文类中被部署（尽管在史学中较少）以支持该信息，无论是要支撑皇帝权威还是要叫他守规矩。
en: In his discussion of the dynamic between emperor and law in the sources for the early Palaiologan period, Dimiter Angelov points out that panegyrical orations tended to proclaim the emperor as above the laws, whereas works in other genres, sometimes written by the same authors, explained the strict requirements for extralegal acts to be legitimate, for example, the practice of recognized virtues such as philanthropy, and that the rights of subjects ought not to be violated.

This division of labor between genres makes sense, as the purpose of panegyrics was to highlight the emperor’s personal virtue, and this was showcased sharply in morally autonomous acts. By contrast, the Mirrors of Princes tended to present the emperor as a mere office-holder who ought to obey the law.

Obeying the law was in itself a praiseworthy choice and corresponded to the imperial virtues of legality and (republican) humility. It is therefore possible to cite panegyrical orations that also take that approach, starting from Pliny on Trajan and going strong in the thirteenth century.

The different genres that we have relied on so far to reconstruct the parameters of the Byzantine republic reflect a single underlying ideology, inflected differently in each genre: legal sources presented the functions of the imperial office just as emperors wanted their subjects to perceive them; panegyrical orations aimed to prove that each occupant of the throne was personally fit for the office; Mirrors of Princes were an externalized form of self-reflection through which emperors acknowledged their duties and recognized the difference between kingship and tyranny; and historiography was the genre in which each emperor was judged by the standards that were proclaimed in the other genres. Religious arguments and rhetoric were deployed in all genres (albeit less so in historiography) to support the message, whether to buttress the emperor’s authority or call him to order.

zh: 不只是文学作品本身，还有它们被表演、呈现与流通的仪式与社会上下文，都起到提醒皇帝其职位之道德与政治目的的作用：皇帝被期望为臣民努力工作，而非通过侵犯臣民权利滥用权力；他们要践行美德、确保正义，且在颁布立法或以非凡方式行动时只追求公共善。皇帝不断被政体道德共识的修辞包围，并被要求内化它、在其官方宣告中自己说出它。在这些文类中没有任何一种把皇帝呈现为许多现代研究中的样子：在辉煌的孤立中，他（或其扩展的天上宫廷）只与上帝处于一种形而上关系。正如保罗·马格达利诺（Paul Magdalino）所写：“我不接受帝国颂词主要是一种宫廷文类而非公民文类：它代表整个
赞美皇帝，而受颂的是皇帝作为共同体首脑的身份。”
加沙的普罗科匹乌斯（Prokopios of Gaza）在一篇当地为尊崇皇帝阿纳斯塔修斯而发表的演说中如此说：“既然城市意识到没有时间让每个人为自己说话，共同体经全体同意（κοινῇ ψήφῳ），满足于演说家的声音。因为他被选中是因为他能代表城市说话，且他以一个声音表达全体的思想。”
在一篇为欧多基亚（Eudokia，公元1068年）所作的演说中，普塞洛斯说他将“通过我的言语表达
（公民）们的声音”，次年他在对罗曼努斯四世（Romanos IV）的致辞中重复了这一主张。
en: Not just the literary works themselves but the ceremonial and social contexts in which they were performed, presented, and circulated served to remind emperors of the moral and political purpose of their office: emperors were expected to work hard on behalf of their subjects, not to abuse their power by transgressing against their subjects’ rights; they were to practice virtue, ensure justice, and pursue only the common good when issuing legislation or acting in extraordinary ways. The emperor was constantly surrounded by the rhetoric of the polity’s moral consensus and was asked to internalize it and speak it himself in his official pronouncements. In none of these genres is the emperor represented as he is in so many modern studies: in splendid isolation, he (or his extended celestial court) engaged only in a metaphysical relationship with God. As Paul Magdalino has written, “I do not accept that imperial panegyric was primarily a court as opposed to a civic genre: it celebrates the emperor on behalf of, and as the head of, the whole

Prokopios of Gaza put it as follows in a speech that he delivered locally to honor the emperor Anastasios: “Since the city realizes that there is not time for each man to speak for himself, the community, by the agreement of all (κοινῇ ψήφῳ), is content with the voice of the orator. For he is chosen for his ability to speak on behalf of the city, and with one voice he expresses the thought of all.”
In an oration for Eudokia (1068 AD), Psellos says that he will “express through my words the voices of the

The idea, for instance, that the emperor had to abide by the laws even though he was not required to was formulated in a specific way: κατὰ νόμους πολιτεύεται, or “he takes part in the

This verb did not mean only to “take part in politics” or “be politically active,” as it is often translated. It meant that one was part of the polity, whether actively or passively, or even that one was “alive.” The Paulician heretics under the emperor Nikephoros I, for example, “were allowed to live in the

This “political” identity of the Byzantines was primary, even in their private lives. In law, when one spouse was captured by barbarians, the other remained “in the

zh: 因此主导意识形态框架在此意义上是共和的。但我们的文本（无论法律还是劝诫）也暗示皇帝有是否服从法律的选择，而劝诫是必要的，因为他们有权力为所欲为。集体政体可以通过其发言人（法学家、演说家、道德顾问）提醒并说服皇帝遵守共识，但这难道不是一种一厢情愿？这些文本中的每一部都暴露一种焦虑：僭主制仅一步之遥，只有君主的意志能防止它。更糟的是，这些君主之镜的流通难道没有为皇帝推行专制政策提供以共和为名的“掩护”，乃至现成的“托词”？毕竟它们不提及任何执行机制，其成功完全依赖个人皈依。
“请对我们好一点”不是共和国的基础。阿塔莱亚特斯在其法律论著中把这一点说穿了。引用皇帝不受法律约束的准则后，他加上这一澄清：“也就是说，如果他违反它们，他不受惩罚。”
en: Therefore, the dominant ideological framework was republican in this sense. But our texts, whether legal or hortatory, also imply that emperors had a choice of whether to obey the laws or not, and exhortation was necessary because they had the power to do as they wished. The collective polity could, through its spokesmen ( jurists, orators, moral advisors), remind and persuade emperors to abide by the consensus, but was this not a form of wishful thinking? Every one of these texts betrays an anxiety that tyranny is but a small step away and only the monarch’s will can prevent it. Worse, did the circulation of these Mirrors not provide republican “cover” or even “alibis” for emperors to pursue absolutist policies? After all, they refer to no enforcement mechanism and rely for their success solely on personal conversion.

“Please be nice to us” is no foundation for a republic. Attaleiates spelled this out in his legal treatise. Citing the precept that the emperor is not subject to the laws, he adds this clarification: “that is to say, he is not punished if he transgresses against them.”

zh: 即使把皇帝视为“专制”君主的历史学家也承认，鉴于前现代技术与通讯，其权力在实践中受严重限制；他们必须通过官僚与精英统治，后者的行事方式不易改变、其支持有时至关重要；
且要成为僭主，一个人必须挣脱那以蜜语包围并窒息该职位的守法、共和统治意识形态。答复请愿与上诉；接见使团；出席宫廷、教会与城市仪式；听取部门首脑报告——这些使皇帝忙于例行工作。要成为僭主，一个人必须找到时间与精力去逆势而行，把这些人与制度弯折到自己的意志，这不可能容易。做僭主可能比做一个正当共和皇帝费工得多，后者只要求顺流而行，即接受共和共识。
en: Even historians who view the emperors as “absolute” monarchs concede that their power was severely limited in practice, given premodern technology and communications; they had to rule through bureaucracies and elites whose ways of doing things were not easy to change and whose support was sometimes crucial;

and, to become a tyrant, one had to break free of the ideology of lawful, republican rule that surrounded and smothered the office in honeyed words. Answering petitions and appeals; receiving embassies; attending court, church, and city ceremonies; and receiving reports from heads of departments kept emperors busy with routine work. To be a tyrant one had to find both the time and energy to go against the grain, to bend these people and institutions to one’s will, which could not have been easy. It was probably much more work to be a tyrant than a proper republican emperor, which required only that one go with the current, that is, accept the republican consensus.

zh: 然而归根结底，强调严格他律的共和观念，其核心却容留着一种彻底的自主性。这个政体的统治者——那个应当保护它、促进其公共善、且站在“共享文化价值体系中心”的人
——也站在那些法律之上。悖谬的是，他只有出于自愿才服从那些法律。只有他自愿，才能让自己的意志服从法律。他被授权以其他罗马人无法采用的方式行动，且与他们相比拥有巨大权力。他的地位不确切是一个官职，尽管可以如此设想；也不太可能清楚区分其生活与权力的私人面向与公共面向，尽管许多拜占庭人声称如此。认为这一地位是共和政治秩序的堡垒与支撑，是一种信仰行为。拜占庭的
都符合那一政治秩序，
最重要、最有权力的东西。
en: Yet when all is said and done, a heart of radical autonomy beat within the republican ideology of strict heteronomy. The ruler of this polity, the person who was supposed to protect it and promote its common good and who stood “at the center of a system of shared cultural values,”

also stood above those laws. It was, perversely, only by an act of his own will that he submitted to those laws. It was only by an act of will that he bent his will to the laws. He was authorized to act in ways available to no other Roman and had immense power compared to them. His position was not exactly a magistracy, though it was possible to think of it as such; nor was it really possible to distinguish clearly between the private and public aspects of his life and power, as many Byzantines claimed to do. To think that this position was a bulwark and support of a republican political order was an act of faith.

for the most important and powerful thing.

zh: 乔治·阿甘本（Giorgio Agamben）写过一部关于“例外状态”的挑战通说的论著，即为应对危机而紧急暂停法律正常运作。虽然他把它理论化为现代自由主义政体的一个特征、且正倾向于成为规则而非例外，他也讨论其罗马先例，包括（尽管只是附带地）皇帝其人。他引用先前理论家，据他们例外状态构成“公共法与政治事实之间的失衡点……法律与政治的交汇”，并得出结论：它“显现为不能具有法律形式之物的法律形式……公共法与政治事实之间的无人之地”。
这种例外状态（罗马皇帝地位是其一种形式）“不是一种特殊法律（如战争法）；相反，就它是法律秩序本身的暂停而言，它界定法律的门槛或极限概念。”
在该点掌权者可能选择也可能不选择适用法律与维护共同价值。皇帝的尴尬地位（“我不受法律约束，但无论如何我会服从它们——除了我不服从的时候”）催生了一种分裂：一派寻求把例外状态纳入法律秩序的范围，另一派视之为外在的、即本质上政治的、或无论如何法外的现象。在前者中，有些人理解它为实在法的组成部分，因为奠定它的必要性充当自主的法律渊源；而另一些人把它构想为国家对其自身保存的主观（自然或宪法）权利。
en: Giorgio Agamben has written a provocative treatise on “the state of exception,” the emergency suspension of the normal operation of law in order to meet a crisis. While he theorizes this as a feature of modern liberal regimes that is tending to become the rule rather than the exception, he discusses also its Roman precedents, including, though only tangentially, the person of the emperor. He quotes previous theorists according to whom the state of exception constitutes a “point of imbalance between public law and political fact... the intersection of the legal and the political,” and concludes that it “appears as the legal form of what cannot have legal form... a no-man’s-land between public law and political fact.”

This state of exception, a form of which was the position of the Roman emperor, “is not a special kind of law (like the law of war); rather, insofar as it is a suspension of the juridical order itself, it defines law’s threshold or limit concept.”

Whoever holds power at that point may or may not choose to apply laws and uphold common values. The emperor’s awkward position (“I am not bound by laws, but will obey them anyway—except when I don’t”) gives rise to a division between those who seek to include the state of exception within the sphere of the juridical order and those who consider it something external, that is, an essentially political, or in any case extrajuridical, phenomenon. Among the former, some understand it to be an integral part of positive law because the necessity that grounds it acts as an autonomous source of law, while others conceive of it as the state’s subjective (natural or constitutional) right to its own preservation.

zh: 这些替代选项恰好对应我们在法律史料中观察到的二分。
en: These alternatives correspond exactly to the bifurcation we observed in the legal sources.

阿甘本就此发出警告（关乎当下，但所用措辞是恺撒时代罗马人也能轻易理解的）：“这种把临时与例外措施转化为治理技术的转变，威胁要根本改变——事实上已明显改变——传统宪制形式之区分的结构与意义”

en: The monarchy had its roots in the chaos of the Republic and the monarch was a way to save the polity from its own systemic flaws, but it provided “an anomic foundation of the juridical order. The identification between sovereign and law represents, that is, the first attempt to assert the anomie of the sovereign and, at the same time, his essential link to the juridical order.”

Agamben warns, in relation to the present but in terms that Romans of the age of Caesar would readily grasp, that “this transformation of a provisional and exceptional measure into a technique of government threatens radically to alter—in fact, has already palpably altered—the structure and meaning of the traditional distinction between constitutional forms”

zh: 那么，当拜占庭由如此一种永久例外状态治理时，如何能坚持它是一个共和国？答案是双重的。第一，共和国的意识形态规范被大多数皇帝接受，或被所有皇帝在大部分时间接受。帝国职位是作为政体的一部分、并在政体关系中以我们探索过的特定罗马方式被构成的。这些规范与其说是职位的
，不如说是其

我们不应从一个证据中无处反映的专制君主制模型出发、然后寻找其限制。相反，我们应主要像所有拜占庭人那样、在守法政体的关系中理解该职位，然后问皇帝在何种情形下、又会怎样扭曲这种关系。毕竟阿甘本的分析主要适用于现代民主政体，其中许多如今处于永久例外状态。我们都想相信我们生活在守法治理的社会，但同时我们的法律恰恰授予机构与权威在某些方面为所欲为而不受惩罚的权力，更不用说掌权者能够行动于法律之外且几乎从不被绳之以法的事实。有些人会论证这些当代社会不再是守法政体，因此不再够格称为民主、共和国或无论什么。
en: How, then, can one maintain that Byzantium was a republic when it was governed by such a permanent state of exception? The answer is twofold. First, the ideological norms of the republic were accepted by most of the emperors, or by all the emperors most of the time. The imperial office was constituted as part of, and in relation to, the polity in the particular Roman ways we have explored. These norms were not so much
on the office as they were its

We should not be starting from a model of absolute monarchy, which is nowhere reflected in the evidence, and then look for its limitations. Rather, we should understand the office primarily the way all Byzantines did, in relation to a lawful polity, and then ask how and under what circumstances it could distort that relation. After all, Agamben’s analysis applies primarily to modern democratic regimes, many of which are now in a permanent state of exception. We all want to believe that we live in societies governed by law but at the same time our very laws grant institutions and authorities the power to do as they please with impunity in certain respects, to say nothing of the fact that people in power are able to act outside the law and are almost never brought to justice. Some would argue that these contemporary societies are no longer lawful polities and so no longer qualify as democracies, republics, or whatever.

children: 皇帝的权力不是政体中唯一的例外状态。

zh: 事实上，政体的其余部分可以暂停其自身的守法参与、并亲手对皇帝采取行动。这也导致一种法外事态的建立，但就像帝国职位本身一样，它也在政体规范之内，因为政体被理解为人民的财产。人民可以收回本来就属于他们的东西。换言之，我们需要重新考虑的是主权者是谁的问题。大多数拜占庭学家假设这是皇帝，但也许我们一直把权力（而且是仅在特定情形下才拥有的权力）与主权混淆。拜占庭史在两种例外状态之间摆动：皇帝的治理与政权更迭的动荡。只有处在两种例外之间的情形才由法律治理（不过，这个“只有”所覆盖的范围很广）。因此当阿塔莱亚特斯说皇帝违法时不受惩罚，他只是作为法学家说话，而非作为他后来将成为的历史学家。皇帝可能不受制于某位美国政治家曾令人困惑地称为“控制性法律权威”的东西，但他却受政治现实制约。在拜占庭，政治行动也可以超出法律范围，具体说就是超出禁止叛国的法律。
可以在其选择时行动于该法（及任何其他法律）之外，因为它归根结底是拜占庭政治领域一切权威的渊源。人民的权威可以压倒皇帝的法律法令。而且不只是

en: The real question, however, is, what consequences do those who govern in a state of exception face when they violate the norms of that republic? This brings us to the second point, the subject of Chapter 4.

children: The power of the emperor was not the only state of exception in the polity.

en: In fact, the rest of the polity could suspend its own lawful participation and take matters into its own hands against the emperors. This too led to the establishment of an extrajuridical state of affairs but one that was, like the imperial office itself, also within the norms of the polity, given that the polity was understood as the property of the people. The people could take back what was theirs to begin with. In other words, what we need to reconsider is the question of who the sovereign was. Most Byzantinists assume that this was the emperor, but perhaps we have been confusing power—and that only under certain circumstances—with sovereignty. The history of Byzantium oscillated between two states of exception: governance by an emperor and the tumult of regime-change. The laws governed only the states in between (though this was a big “only”). Therefore, when Attaleiates said that the emperor is not punished when he breaks the law, he was speaking only as a jurist, not the historian that he would become. The emperor may not have been subject to what an American politician once confusingly called “a controlling legal authority,” but he was subject to political fact, and that fact in Byzantium could also operate outside the law, more specifically the law against treason. rebels too could appeal to the higher law of the common good of the republic when they set aside the laws of treason and their own oaths of loyalty.

zh: 让我们以我们开始时的文类结束。执事阿加佩托斯（Agapetos）致查士丁尼一系列道德格言，其中有以下一条：“你须自定守法的义务，因为人世间无人能强使你守法。”
但后一条格言是不祥的：“臣民甘愿接受你的统治，你才能自认为统治稳固。因为不愿意的臣民一有机会就反叛。而被善意纽带统治的人，对其统治者的服从是牢固的。”
在其他上下文中，此类语言被读作“隐含的暴力威胁与恭敬的致辞语气”的结合。
en: Let us close with the genre with which we began. The deacon Agapetos addressed a series of moral maxims to Justinian among which was the following: “Impose on yourself the necessity of keeping the laws, since you have on earth no one able to compel you.”

But a later maxim is ominous: “Consider yourself to rule safely when you rule willing subjects. For the unwilling subject rebels when he has the opportunity. But he who is ruled by the bonds of goodwill is firm in his obedience to his ruler.”
In other contexts, such language has been read as a combination of “an implicit threat of violence and a deferential tone of address.”
